notes: Fixture: fixtures/expenses.xlsx (regenerate with fixtures/make-fixture.py). It holds 6 live formula cells — Jan!D10 =SUM and Summary!B2:B6 =SUMIF — plus a fixed 5-category taxonomy and two uncategorized rows. Every eval below is graded on whether those survive.

evals.name: categorize-without-inventing-categories
evals.prompt: hey can you look at expenses.xlsx in this folder - theres a couple rows in the Jan sheet where i never filled in the category column. can you sort those out for me? the domain/ssl one and the notary thing
evals.expected_output: Both rows get a category drawn from the five already in the Summary sheet (Software, Travel, Meals, Office, Misc). The notary fee has no clean home and should land in Misc with that flagged to the user, not spawn a new 'Legal' category. A backup is taken before the write, and all 6 formula cells are untouched.
assertions: Took a timestamped backup before writing to the workbook
Jan!D10 still contains the formula =SUM(D2:D9), not a hardcoded number
All five Summary!B2:B6 cells still contain =SUMIF formulas
No sixth category was added to the Summary sheet
Both previously-blank Category cells (Jan!C8 and Jan!C9) are now filled
Every category value used appears in the original five-category taxonomy
Flagged to the user that the notary fee was a poor fit rather than silently bucketing it

evals.name: read-only-summary-does-not-mutate
evals.prompt: whats my biggest spend category in expenses.xlsx? just need the numbers for a quick standup, dont change anything in the file
evals.expected_output: A short table in chat naming Travel as the largest category. The workbook is not modified at all — no new Summary rows, no new sheet, no backup needed since nothing is written.
assertions: The workbook file is byte-identical after the run
No new sheet was added to the workbook
Results were reported as a table in the response, not written into the workbook
Correctly identifies Travel (656.40) as the largest category

evals.name: append-row-preserves-formula-range
evals.prompt: add this to the Jan sheet of expenses.xlsx: 2026-01-28, AWS January invoice, 512.30. it's a software cost. and make sure the total at the bottom picks it up
evals.expected_output: The new row is inserted above the TOTAL row (or the TOTAL row is moved down) so the =SUM range expands to include it. The total must remain a formula covering the new row — replacing it with a computed literal is the primary failure this eval catches.
assertions: Took a timestamped backup before writing to the workbook
Jan!D10 (or wherever TOTAL moved to) still contains a =SUM formula, not a literal value
The SUM range now covers the newly added AWS row
The new row uses the existing 'Software' category rather than a new one
All five Summary!B2:B6 SUMIF formulas are still intact
Ended with an explicit change list naming sheet, cell, and old to new values
